title: Avoiding Double Sanitary Tees on Horizontal Waste Lines
description: Connecting two back-to-back fixtures using a standard double sanitary tee on a horizontal waste line is a frequent error in drainage installations. When waste discharges from one side, the straight cross-entry allows fluid and debris to shoot straight across into the opposite fixture rather than turning downstream. Most model plumbing codes prohibit double sanitary tees in horizontal-to-horizontal applications. Instead, installers should use a double combination wye and eighth bend or a double fixture fitting (often called a figure-five fitting). These fittings provide a smooth, directional sweep that prevents crossover and maintains proper flow.

Avoiding Double Sanitary Tees on Horizontal Waste Lines

Connecting two back-to-back fixtures using a standard double sanitary tee on a horizontal waste line is a frequent error in drainage installations. Most model plumbing codes prohibit double sanitary tees in horizontal-to-horizontal applications. Instead, installers should use a double combination wye and eighth bend or a double fixture fitting (often called a figure-five fitting). These fittings provide a smooth, directional sweep that prevents crossover and maintains proper flow.
